chapter: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
title: How Billie Holiday worked with the band, and her drinking
summary: She kept time with her feet, never interfered if she trusted you, and asked tactfully for balance fixes. She drank and used drugs, which did not hurt her singing, and nobody dared deny her.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: How was she to work with? I mean, for instance, like when you're rehearsing, or --

She would sit back and listen, you know. If she knew you knew what you were doing, she would never interfere, you know. And if you did something that really pleased her, and have the band do something, you could like at the expression on her face, and you could tell that she tell you thank you that way, you know. As long as you got the right tempo for her, she was fine, and I used to start the band out, especially the big bands that we would use -- she would wear these long dresses, and her feet would keep tempo. She'd just do like that, and she had the beat -- she would never drop time or anything else, and she always had presence of mind. If something went wrong, a guy was too loud behind her, one of those things, she'd go right on through the performance. Then after, she'd come and tell me -- "Have the trumpet player turned a little bit." You know, It's in my ear a little bit. Just bothers me -- just a little." But she was so diplomatic in even asking that
Did -- was she drinking a lot at that time, or --
Well, she drank, let's put it this way. She drank, and some other things, you know.
Was she pretty spacey or was she pretty much there? I mean, when you talked with her, did she --

She had her faculties. It didn't seem to bother her. It seemed like she really needed this. It got so she depended upon it. But it didn't affect her singing, like I've seen it affect some people, you know. And it was a pitiful situation, but you were afraid to deny her these things, because you don't know what it might have done, you know, to her. So as long as she performed and did a great performance, you just couldn't disturb her.
